interest: This document provides valuable insight into the Japanese government's industrial policy during the early years of the Great Depression, specifically the operations of the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau (Rinji Sangyō Gōrikakyoku) created in 1930 under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It illustrates how Japanese authorities and industrial leaders sought to overcome economic distress by coordinating production, rationalizing sales, and pursuing corporate amalgamation within the domestic woolen textile sector. While the file in this collection is a single List of Papers cross-reference sheet, it serves as an indispensable index pointing researchers to Edwin L. Neville's broader political reporting (894.00 P.R./32) on interwar Japanese economic reorganization.
overview: This file consists of a single-page State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.62222, covering the subject of sheep, goats, and wool in Japan for 1930. The sole recorded entry, dated August 1, 1930, cross-references political report No. 219 sent from Japan by Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville (originally filed under 894.00 P.R./32). The purport outlines the proceedings of the first meeting of the woolen industry committee under the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau held in July 1930, which evaluated the rationalization of production and marketing along with fundamental industry reorganization through the amalgamation of woolen manufacturing enterprises.

subfiles.summary: This document is a List of Papers docket sheet for decimal file 894.62222 (Sheep. Goats. Wool - Japan) dated August 1, 1930. It records a single cross-reference entry to report No. 219 from Edwin L. Neville in Japan, filed under 894.00 P.R./32. The entry summarizes the initial July 1930 meeting of the woolen industry committee of the Temporary Industrial Rationalization Bureau, which examined the rationalization of production and sales as well as the proposed amalgamation of firms in the wool manufacturing industry.
